5-4.title: Use Area Models to Multiply Multi-Digit Factors

questions.title: Be Curious · What do you see?
questions.hint: Look at how the big tray is split into smaller sections.
steps: Look at the whole bento box. What shape is it?
Notice how it is divided into smaller rectangles.
Tell what you notice, like how many sections there are or how the parts fit together.
questions.answer: Sample answer: I see a rectangular lunch box divided into smaller rectangles. The small sections fit together to make the whole box, so their areas add up to the area of the whole box.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; opinion/noticing prompt with no single answer.

questions.title: Math is… Mindset
questions.hint: This is a reflection about working with a partner, not a one-answer problem.
steps: Think about a time your partner explained an idea.
What could you say or do to show you really listened?
Write one way you can show it.
questions.answer: Sample answer: I can repeat my partner's idea in my own words and ask a question about it before I share my own idea.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; reflection prompt with no single answer.

questions.title: Learn · 72 × 114 soccer field
questions.hint: Break 72 into tens and ones and 114 into hundreds, tens and ones.
questions.answer: Top row: 7,000 | 700 | 280; bottom row: 200 | 20 | 8. 72 × 114 = 8,208, so the area is 8,208 square feet.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 72 × 114 = 8,208; sum of six partial products also 8,208; matches the page.

questions.title: Math is… Modeling
questions.hint: Think about what each small box in the area model stands for.
steps: Look at how the big rectangle is split into smaller boxes.
Each box is one partial product.
Explain how adding the boxes gives the whole product.
questions.answer: Sample answer: An area model breaks a big multiplication into smaller, easier products by place value. Each small box is a partial product, and adding them gives the area of the whole rectangle, which is the product.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; explanation prompt with no single answer.

questions.title: Work Together · 304 × 68
steps: Draw a rectangle with 300 + 4 across the top and 60 + 8 down the side.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 304 × 68 = 20,672; partial products 18,000 + 2,400 + 240 + 32 = 20,672; estimate 300 × 70 = 21,000.

questions.title: Problem 1 · Area model for 154 × 36
questions.hint: Each empty box is the side number on its row times the top number of its column.
steps: Multiply row by column for each empty box: 30 × 50 = 1,500, 30 × 4 = 120, 6 × 50 = 300, 6 × 4 = 24.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 154 × 36 = 5,544; partial products sum to 5,544; estimate 150 × 36 = 5,400.

questions.title: Problem 2 · Area model for 421 × 52
questions.hint: The top row is 50 times each part; the bottom row is 2 times each part.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 421 × 52 = 21,892; partial products sum to 21,892; estimate 400 × 50 = 20,000.

questions.title: Problem 3 · 15 × 24
steps: Draw lines in the box to make 4 smaller boxes.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 15 × 24 = 360; partial products sum to 360; check 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

questions.title: Problem 4 · 28 × 132
steps: Divide the long box into 2 rows and 3 columns.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 28 × 132 = 3,696; six partial products sum to 3,696; check 3,696 ÷ 28 = 132.

questions.title: Problem 5 · 33 × 78
steps: Sketch an area model with 2 rows and 2 columns.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 33 × 78 = 2,574; partial products sum to 2,574; estimate 30 × 80 = 2,400.

questions.title: Problem 6 · 72 × 225
steps: Sketch an area model with 2 rows and 3 columns.
Add all six: the total is 16,200.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 72 × 225 = 16,200; six partial products sum to 16,200; check 16,200 ÷ 72 = 225.

questions.title: Problem 7 · Area model 218 × 28
questions.hint: Add the numbers on top to get one factor and the numbers on the side to get the other.
steps: Top: 200 + 10 + 8 = 218. Side: 20 + 8 = 28. So the equation is 218 × 28.
Fill the boxes: 4,000 | 200 | 160 on top and 1,600 | 80 | 64 on the bottom.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 218 × 28 = 6,104; six partial products sum to 6,104; estimate 200 × 30 = 6,000.

questions.title: Problem 8 · Area model 416 × 63
questions.hint: Add the numbers on top to get one factor and the numbers on the side to get the other.
steps: Top: 400 + 10 + 6 = 416. Side: 60 + 3 = 63. So the equation is 416 × 63.
Fill the boxes: 24,000 | 600 | 360 on top and 1,200 | 30 | 18 on the bottom.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 416 × 63 = 26,208; six partial products sum to 26,208; estimate 400 × 60 = 24,000.

questions.title: Problem 9 · Football field area
questions.hint: Area of a rectangle is length × width.
steps: The field is 120 yards long and 53 yards wide.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 120 × 53 = 6,360; partial products 6,000 + 360; check 6,360 ÷ 53 = 120.

questions.title: Problem 10 · Canned food
questions.hint: Multiply the number of boxes by the cans in each box.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 128 × 45 = 5,760; partial products 5,120 + 640; estimate 130 × 45 = 5,850.

questions.title: Problem 11 · STEM Connection · Owen's sketchbooks
questions.hint: Multiply the number of sketchbooks by the sketches in each one.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 14 × 128 = 1,792; partial products 1,280 + 512; check 1,792 ÷ 14 = 128.

questions.title: Problem 12 · Extend Your Thinking · 452 × 273
questions.hint: Break both factors into hundreds, tens and ones.
steps: Draw a rectangle with 400 + 50 + 2 on one side and 200 + 70 + 3 on the other, making 9 boxes.
Add all nine partial products to get 123,396.
questions.answer: Sample answer: Break 452 into 400 + 50 + 2 and 273 into 200 + 70 + 3. Make a 3-by-3 area model and multiply to get 9 partial products: 80,000 + 28,000 + 1,200 + 10,000 + 3,500 + 150 + 400 + 140 + 6 = 123,396. So 452 × 273 = 123,396.
questions.verification: Computed in Python; 452 × 273 = 123,396; nine partial products sum to 123,396; estimate 450 × 270 = 121,500.

Think about how the area model kept your partial products organized.
Write how you checked that your answer made sense.
questions.answer: Sample answer: I broke each factor into hundreds, tens and ones, used an area model to find each partial product, added them, and checked with an estimate.
